headline: Highest risk is cascading error: Haystack can consume Airflow-produced outputs via MCP/REST and act on them without verification, while both also expose broad network egress.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airflow has broad network egress but no browser or shared channel documented; Haystack explicitly uses MCP servers and REST APIs, so if Airflow writes attacker-controlled content into a shared workspace or API payload, Haystack could parse it as instructions. The pairwise bridge is inferred, not directly evidenced, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF Airflow outputs are routed into a shared file, queue, or MCP endpoint that Haystack reads
IF Haystack treats retrieved content as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Disable any shared workspace or queue between the two agents
Add provenance tags to Airflow outputs before Haystack reads them
Require Haystack to strip instruction-like text from retrieved content
Use allowlisted schemas for any Airflow-to-Haystack handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airflow touches no declared sensitive data classes, while Haystack only lists anonymous usage statistics. Both have broad network egress, but there is no documented shared filesystem, OAuth principal, or PHI/secret handling. The leakage pathway is therefore limited and not evidenced as a default data-class spill.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace containing sensitive files
IF either agent is configured to ingest those files into its inference backend
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Remove sensitive files from any shared directory
Restrict outbound destinations with an allowlist
Turn off telemetry where possible

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airflow is a data orchestrator with broad network egress, and Haystack can call REST APIs and MCP servers, so they can overlap on mutable external resources. However, neither profile shows unrestricted filesystem write, git mutation, or shared OAuth scopes, so the conflict is plausible but not high-blast-radius.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same external API, database, or queue
IF no locking or idempotency checks are added around those writes
mitigations: Assign separate target resources to each agent
Add idempotency keys to writes
Serialize writes through one orchestrator
Enable resource-level locking where available

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airflow can generate pipeline outputs that Haystack may ingest through REST or MCP, and Haystack is a search/RAG agent that may treat retrieved content as authoritative. No verification step is documented in either profile, so the pair can propagate errors by default when chained, though not enough evidence supports high severity.
conditions: IF Haystack consumes Airflow-produced artifacts as source material
IF Haystack forwards those artifacts into downstream answers or actions without verification
mitigations: Insert a validation step between Airflow and Haystack
Require citations or source hashes for any forwarded facts
Mark Airflow outputs as untrusted by default
Sample-check a few outputs before enabling automation

E_compliance.rationale: Airflow has no declared data classes touched, while Haystack only lists anonymous usage statistics, so there is no direct residency or regulated-data mismatch evidenced here. The main compliance concern is telemetry/retention drift if both are deployed under different policies, which is a limited gap rather than a default breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is later routed through either agent
IF their logging or retention settings differ for the same dataset
mitigations: Document retention settings for both agents
Disable unnecessary telemetry
Keep regulated data out of the pair until policies are reviewed
Align log deletion schedules
